question: Which keyboard shortcut builds and runs the current scheme in Xcode?
explanation: ⌘R runs the app (building first if needed); ⌘B only builds, ⌘. stops, and ⌘U runs tests.

question: Which keyboard shortcut builds the project without running it?
explanation: ⌘B builds without launching; ⌘R would also run it, ⌘K cleans the build folder, and ⌘U runs tests.

question: The app is running in the Simulator and you want to stop the currently running scheme. Which shortcut does that?
explanation: ⌘. stops the running app in Xcode; ⌘Q would quit Xcode itself and ⌘W closes a window/tab.

question: Which keyboard shortcut runs the test suite?
explanation: ⌘U runs the tests; ⌘R runs the app, ⌘B builds, and ⌘T opens a new tab.

question: You want to jump straight to a file or symbol by typing part of its name. Which shortcut opens the "Open Quickly" search?
explanation: ⌘⇧O opens "Open Quickly" for fuzzy file/symbol search; ⌘O opens a file from disk and ⌘⇧F is project-wide find.

question: Which navigator shows the files and groups that make up your project?
explanation: The Project navigator lists the project's files and groups; the others focus on debugging, issues, and breakpoints respectively.

question: Your app is paused at a breakpoint and you want to inspect the call stack along with the live CPU and memory gauges. Which navigator do you use?
explanation: The Debug navigator shows the thread/call-stack and the performance gauges while the app is running or paused.

question: After a build fails, you want a single scrollable list of every compiler warning and error to click through. Which navigator gives you that?
explanation: The Issue navigator collects all build warnings and errors in one place, and clicking one jumps to the offending line.

question: Which navigator lets you see and manage all of the breakpoints across your project in one list?
explanation: The Breakpoint navigator lists every breakpoint in the project and lets you enable, disable, edit, or delete them.

question: You want to rename a type and have every reference to it updated safely throughout the project. What is the right approach?
options: Manually find-and-replace the text in each file
Delete the type and retype it everywhere
Rename only the file in Finder
explanation: The Rename refactoring understands the code and updates the declaration together with all references, unlike error-prone manual text replacement.

question: When you apply Xcode's Rename refactoring to a method, what happens?
options: The declaration and all of its call sites are updated together
explanation: Rename is symbol-aware, so it changes the declaration and every place the method is called in one coordinated edit.

question: You have selected a repeated block of code and want Xcode to pull it into its own method, replacing the selection with a call to that new method. Which refactoring action does this?
explanation: Extract to Method moves the selected code into a new function and replaces the selection with a call to it, reducing duplication.

question: You Command-click a function name in the source editor. What does Xcode do?
options: Jumps to the definition of that symbol
explanation: Command-clicking a symbol navigates directly to its definition (jump-to-definition).

question: The horizontal bar at the top of the editor that shows the path (project > group > file > symbol) and lets you click any part to navigate is called the:
explanation: The jump bar sits atop the editor and lets you navigate by clicking any element of the path, including individual symbols in the current file.

question: After Command-clicking to jump to a definition in another file, which action returns you to where you were before?
explanation: Navigate Back (⌃⌘←) returns to your previous editing location; Undo would instead revert text edits, which is unrelated to navigation history.
